payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image reliably show that the source blue mug itself was moved to the right of the headphones, rather than remaining at its former position while a different mug is on the right?
node.criteria: Compare the source blue mug, including its distinctive body and handle, with objects in the edited image and assess its position relative to the same headphones. Pass only when visual evidence reliably supports that the source mug itself is now to the right of the headphones. Fail only when evidence reliably establishes that the source mug was not moved there. Use unknown when blur, appearance changes, or other ambiguity prevents reliable determination of the source mug's identity or movement. A mug appearing on the right alone does not establish that the source mug was moved.
node.binding: Cross-image binding: the blue mug in the source image and the same headphones in the source and edited images; compare the source mug with the edited mugs and assess the source mug's position relative to the headphones in the edited image, allowing for changes in scale, lighting, and appearance.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows two small mugs: one to the left of the headphones and one to their right. Neither clearly retains the source mug’s distinctive blue body and left-facing handle; the blue-looking area at the former position is heavily blurred and does not establish the mug’s identity or movement. Thus the right-side mug alone is insufficient to determine whether the source mug was moved there.

d2: The current binding and criterion test only whether any mug is right of the headphones, so the trace passes on the rightmost mug even though the edited image also shows a mug left of the headphones and a blurred blue remnant where the original mug was. That establishes some progress, not complete fulfillment; the aggregate/reference mismatch likely reflects that this single binary check cannot distinguish partial from complete. For typed structural edits, preserve the final-image spatial check but make its scope and output semantics explicit: assess all visible mugs and their positions, and distinguish a clearly supported partial result from complete fulfillment only when the node has evidence relevant to the requested move (including source-to-edited comparison). Do not infer that the rightmost mug is the moved source mug from the edited image alone. Keep uncertainty for ambiguous object identity or position; the trace is valid, queried, and has no dependency or transport failure, so this is a criterion/coverage limitation rather than a visual-evidence or execution failure.
